summary: Ferdinand von Eckstein worked in Indology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Göttingen and at Heidelberg University under Friedrich Creuzer (ca. 1810–1812), and later served as a member of the Société Asiatique (ca. 1822–1861).

Ferdinand von Richthofen was a scholar in history and archaeology. After studying at the University of Breslau (ca. 1850–1853) and Humboldt University of Berlin (ca. 1853–1856), he held posts at Bonn (ca. 1875–1883), Leipzig (ca. 1883–1886), and Berlin (ca. 1886–1905).

Ferdinando Belloni-Filippi specialized in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Pisa under Francesco Lorenzo Pullè and Carlo Formichi (ca. 1897–1901) and at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi (1909). He held professorships at Pisa and Florence.

Ferenc Ruzsa works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fazekas Mihály Gimnázium (ca. 1971–1975) and Eötvös Loránd University (ca. 1976–1982), where he later held a post around 1986.

Fernand Brunner was a philosophy scholar. He completed his licence ès lettres at the University of Lausanne (ca. 1938–1942) and a Ph.D. at the University of Paris (ca. 1945–1951), later holding posts at the University of Neuchâtel and University of Bern.

Fernand Grenard worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Sciences Po / École Libre des Sciences Politiques (ca. 1886–1889) and at INALCO / École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (ca. 1887–1890).

Fernand Meyer is a Tibetology scholar. He held appointments at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique, the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2004), and the Helmholtz Centre for Infection Research (2016).
Fernando Jose Benetti is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Nalanda University, completing doctoral research supervised by Aleksandra Wenta (attested 2018).

Fernando Tola worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy after studying at the National University of San Marcos. He served as a professor at the University of Buenos Aires (attested 1989) and as director of the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (ca. 1988–2017).
Filip Rucinski specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 2000 to 2006 and completed an M.A. at the University of Warsaw in 2009.

Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Moscow State University, Tübingen, Berlin, Leipzig, and Paris under scholars including Petrov, Roth, Weber, and Curtius, and subsequently became a professor at Moscow State University and member of the Russian Academy of Sciences.
Filippo De Filippi was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the University of Genoa and the University of Bologna.

Filippo Marsili works in sinology and history and archaeology. He studied as a graduate student at the University of California, Berkeley, and under Patricia Berger, Corrado Pensa, Arcangela Santoro, and Paolo Daffinà. He held a post at Saint Louis University (attested 2019).
Finnian M. M. Gerety is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned a PhD at Harvard under Michael Witzel. He has held positions at Yale, Brown University, and the University of Oxford.

Fitzedward Hall was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and Harvard. He held professorships at Government College University, Lahore, Sanskrit College and University, and King's College London, and served as librarian to the India Office (1864–1869).

Flavio Geisshuesler is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned degrees from the University of Lausanne, University of Bern, and University of Virginia under David Germano, later holding posts at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and the University of Sydney.
Flora Blanchon was a scholar who studied under Léon Vandermeersch and Nicole Vandier-Nicolas, and she taught Jacques Giès.

Florin Deleanu works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bucharest, Waseda University, Peking University, and the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, later holding posts at Kansai Medical University, Hamburg, ICPBS, and IIBS.

Florinda De Simini is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Turin. She has held posts at the International Institute for Asian Studies, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Naples "L'Orientale".

Fokke Sierksma was a scholar of religious studies and Tibetology. He earned a Ph.D. at the University of Groningen (1936–1950), worked at its library (ca. 1948–1956), and later served as a lecturer and professor of history of religion at Leiden University.
